result.scope_note: The congressional pay amendment (originally proposed as the Madison Amendment in 1789) was ratified in 1992, requiring 203 years. The original Bill of Rights (first ten amendments) were proposed in 1789 and ratified in 1791, requiring approximately 2 years. This comparison establishes the congressional pay amendment took significantly longer for ratification.

excerpts.text: In the fall of 1789, the First Congress submitted the first constitutional amendments to the states for ratification.

By 1791 the states had ratified [10 of those amendments](/about/origins-foundations/senate-and-constitution/constitution.htm#amdt_1_(1791)), which became known as the Bill of Rights. Unlike recent amendments, with set time limits for ratification, the first 12 amendments were open ended. So in 1992 the states ratified one more of those originally proposed amendments, 203 years after it was submitted to the states.
